profiles.name: HamSammich
profiles.tagline: TEE BOX DRAMA, GREEN SIDE TAXES
profiles.profile: This dude lives in a weird split-brain world where the driver shows up with a shovel and the putter keeps him from getting buried. The ball can clearly travel, but the rest of the bag keeps tripping over its own shoelaces, especially around and on the greens. There’s enough bite off the tee to keep him dangerous for a stretch, then the short game walks in and sets the kitchen on fire. When it clicks, it’s ugly in a useful way: survive first, ask questions later.

profiles.name: DREADFUL
profiles.profile: He’s basically a full-contact exercise in surviving bad golf. The profile says the same thing over and over: tee it somewhere, miss a bunch, chip a bunch, then let the putter try to clean up the mess like a guy mopping floodwater with a spoon. The long game is usually the problem, but the real comedy is how often the whole round turns into a three-putt festival with bonus paperwork. If he’s in the mix, it’s usually because the rest of the field also brought gasoline.

profiles.name: IUDoc92
profiles.profile: This bag is a crime scene with a couple of clean fingerprints on it. The pattern is pretty clear: the tee ball and especially the short game spend most of their time dragging the whole operation into the ditch, while the approach play occasionally remembers it’s allowed to help. There are enough flashes to keep him from being a total clown show, but the volatility is baked in. One stretch looks like survival golf, the next looks like the clubs are being negotiated with through a translator.

profiles.name: TEV_11
profiles.tagline: APPROACH GAME IN THE MIDDLE OF A RANSOM NOTE
profiles.profile: The odd thing here is that the driver can occasionally behave, the short game can absolutely pop, and then the approach play walks in wearing work boots and ruins the carpet. That’s the whole identity: enough pieces show up to make him dangerous, but the iron game is the recurring punchline. When he’s on, it’s because the front end of the bag isn’t actively sabotaging him. When he’s off, the misses are loud enough to need a permit.

profiles.name: MashedBROtato
profiles.profile: This profile is pure chaos with a little upside sprinkled on top like hot sauce on a turd. He can absolutely let it rip, and every so often the whole thing catches fire and looks legitimately nasty in a good way, but the rest of the time the approach/short-game combo turns the round into a recovery clinic. The putter is usually the least offensive part, which is wild considering how often the tee-to-green stuff gets mugged in an alley. He’s the kind of player who can win ugly and also lose spectacularly on the same postcard.

profiles.name: Jakobm90
profiles.tagline: TEE SHOT ARSONIST, PATCHY REPAIR MAN
profiles.profile: This guy is all boom-and-bust in the same dirty sweater. The driver tends to create the mess, the irons don’t always bail him out, and then somehow the short game will show up like a guy who got lost on the way to another tee time. That makes the file volatile: one look says “please stop hitting it sideways,” the next says he can scramble out of a dumpster fire and still hang around. It’s not clean golf, but it is often interesting, which is the best and worst thing you can say about a golfer.
